selected.title: Mirror-image molecules: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai
verified_facts: R-(-)-carvone smells of spearmint; its mirror image S-(+)-carvone gives caraway seeds their smell (Wikipedia Carvone, LibreTexts Stereoisomerism and Smell)
Mirror-image molecules have the same atoms/bonds, related like left and right hands (Al Jazeera, LibreTexts, Wikipedia Homochirality)
Smell receptors are chiral, so they respond differently to the two forms (Wikipedia Carvone, LibreTexts)
Nearly all protein amino acids are left-handed (L) (Wikipedia Homochirality, arXiv 2110.01975, Al Jazeera 'living organisms use almost exclusively one version')
Ordinary lab reactions give an equal (racemic) mix of both forms (Wikipedia Homochirality, Solar Daily 'How life shatters the chemistry mirror')
Soai reaction: a chiral molecule catalyses its own formation with the same handedness - asymmetric autocatalysis (Soai TUS page, PMC6541725 Symmetry 2019 review, Nobel citation 'autocatalysis')
~0.00005% ee amplified to >99.5% ee (Soai TUS recent-e page, PMC6541725 / DOAJ Symmetry 2019 review)
Kagan: non-linear effect - product ee higher than linear prediction from an impure (scalemic) catalyst (Wikipedia Non-linear effects, Illinois Todd.pdf review)

Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 to Kagan and Soai, announced Oct 7, 'for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis' (nobelprize.org, Al Jazeera, Khaleej Times, ADN/AP, Times of Israel)
Work decisive for pharmaceutical manufacturing / medicines (Khaleej Times/Nobel committee, ABC/AP quoting ACS president, Al Jazeera)
